title: Sea Bream Crudo, Tuberous Begonia Ice & Purslane
notes: Shio-koji is specially fermented rice that is used as a seasoning in Japanese cooking. It adds a soft salty sweet umami flavour to dishes and is often used as a substitute to salt. It is available at good Japanese grocers and speciality stores.

ingredientSections.heading: Begonia Ice
items: 10 Tuberous Begonia Flowers, all same colour, white or yellow preferred

ingredientSections.heading: Cucumber
items: ½ Cup Cucumber, brunoise (very finely diced)

ingredientSections.heading: To Plate
items: Fresh Tuberous Begonia Petals, mixed colours

methodSections.heading: Bream
steps: Slice the bream very thinly, arrange nicely on serving plates, wrap in plastic and set in fridge.

methodSections.heading: Begonia Ice
steps: Blend the flowers, salt and water thoroughly.
Strain through a fine sieve and freeze in a bowl.
Just before serving scrape with a fork to create ice shavings.

methodSections.heading: Garlic
steps: Slice the garlic paper-thin and then mix with the other ingredients.

methodSections.heading: Cucumber
steps: Whisk all ingredients together well and then strain before serving.

methodSections.heading: To Plate
steps: Remove the chilled plates and bream from the fridge. Lightly sprinkle the fish with Maldon salt.
Place a scattering of cucumber on top of the fish and top this with a few pieces of the garlic.
Drizzle with a dash of olive oil and place a few drops of shio-koji on the fish.
Decorate with the petals and purslane. These are the acid component of the dish.
Top with begonia ice shavings and serve immediately.
